verified.entry_point: The real product server: core.New builds the same dependency graph, route registration, authentication middleware, native RBAC, services, persistence and plugin schema loading a deployed Perses uses, and the tests speak HTTP to it. A local HTTP upstream service records the method, path and the credential headers it receives, so a credential that is put to use is observed directly. The plugin archives (Prometheus datasource + Markdown panel) are baked into the verifier image at /opt/perses-plugins. Reproduced on the pinned+injected tree: 14 security tests fail (the unreadable credential reaches the upstream, or the authoring request is accepted) and 12 functional tests plus the project's own internal/api/impl/proxy tests pass; on the reference fix all pass.

verified.project_tests_run: internal/api/impl/proxy: proxy_test.go, readonly_query_test.go, sql_response_test.go, restored from pristine pinned copies over /workspace at grading time and run with the project's native Go runner as uid 1000 (group functional/project.xml). They pass on the pinned+injected tree and on the reference fix; the SQL/read-only/TLS unit cases do not start a server or need the network.
injected_siblings: S1 - internal/api/impl/proxy/proxy.go:178 + internal/api/impl/proxy/ephemeraldatasource.go:41: a saved proxy route for ephemeral dashboards' local datasources; the real upstream ephemeral dashboard service never checks Secret read on create/update. The published fix never touches proxy.go, core/server.go or the ephemeral dashboard service.

S2 - internal/api/impl/proxy/proxy.go:281 (resolveHeaderSecrets): an HTTP proxy header value may reference a stored secret with {{secret:NAME}} and the resolver decrypts it through the same retrieve callback. The published fix never touches proxy.go, and its per-service switch only inspects the proxy's secret field.

wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the guard asks the same authorization authority every other endpoint uses and resolves the credential from persistence; there is no lookup whose absence grants access, and a missing secret produces no credential to use.

traps.lever_type: where (three one-shot proxy entry points) + how (the body is a one-shot reference, not saved configuration)
traps.shape: an unsaved proxy body whose datasource spec names a stored secret, on the project, global and dashboard routes
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a one-shot body persists nothing, so the check looks like it belongs where datasources are saved, and each route sits in its own handler
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the route and the owner check are exactly as published

traps.lever_type: how (a route where the protection never existed) + where (second copy for the global scope)
traps.shape: create/update of a project or global datasource whose spec names a secret the caller cannot read
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the CRUD services already pass a Datasource/GlobalDatasource RBAC check, so saving a datasource looks authorised and the report is about the proxy
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published fix protects exactly these services, which are a different package from the report's landing point

traps.lever_type: how (a producer the report never mentions) + where (separate resource package)
traps.shape: a dashboard or dashboard update whose local datasource specs name a project secret, used later through the saved dashboard datasource proxy
traps.reason_to_dismiss: dashboards are a separate resource with their own RBAC (DashboardScope) and the advisory talks about datasources, so the dashboard save path reads as out of scope
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit; the published fix does not touch the dashboard service

traps.pattern: B (injected sibling S1: route where the protection never existed)
traps.lever_type: how (a producer in another package reached by a sibling sink)
traps.shape: an ephemeral dashboard whose local datasource specs name a project secret, used through the saved ephemeral-dashboard datasource proxy route
traps.reason_to_dismiss: ephemeral dashboards are short-lived previews, and the sink is a route that only exists in our copy, so a solver who fixes dashboards may treat the dashboard resource as the whole set
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream producer (the ephemeral dashboard service) reached by an injected sibling route a maintainer could plausibly have added next to the dashboard proxy route; the published fix touches neither

traps.pattern: B (injected sibling S2: a reference form the plausible check never inspects)
traps.lever_type: how (shape trap: the credential is named inside a value the resolver reads, not in the proxy's secret field)
traps.shape: an HTTP proxy header value containing {{secret:NAME}}, on an unsaved request and in a saved datasource or dashboard
traps.where: internal/api/impl/proxy/proxy.go:281 (resolveHeaderSecrets), reached from newProxy at proxy.go:226
traps.reason_to_dismiss: header values look like plain forwarding configuration, and the report's example names a credential object, so a check written against the datasource's secret field looks complete
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling (our copy only): a header templating feature a maintainer could plausibly add, resolving through the same secret-retrieval callback the proxy already uses; the published fix never touches proxy.go
